title: Proper adic direct image preserves coproducts on the hull
statement:
Fix a universe u, a prime $\ell$, and a field $k$ in universe u of positive
characteristic different from $\ell$. Let $Z,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes
and let $g:Z\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be
a commutative condensed ring with its specified multiplication and a certificate
of one of the three adic coefficient families [def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate].
For $T=Z,Y$, put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$, let $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$
be the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category
[sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], let $\mathcal B_T$ be its bounded constructible
full subcategory [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], and let
$\mathcal L_T=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal B_T)$ be the full localizing hull, using
ambient coproducts indexed in universe u+1
[def-sfb-bounded-constructible-localizing-closure].
Let $i_Z:\mathcal L_Z\to D_Z$ be the full inclusion and let
$Rg_*:D_Z\to D_Y$ be the actual total right derived module-object pushforward.
For every type I in universe u+1, the functor $Rg_*\circ i_Z$ preserves
I-indexed coproducts. Preservation refers to the canonical comparison induced by
the coprojections, including I empty. No claim is made about arbitrary objects
of $D_Z$.

source.place: Parts (1)-(2): coproduct preservation of the identity-compactification functor.

proof.text: The standing schemes and locally closed strata are Noetherian. Identify the local finite presentations in Lean with the adic local models: for E and Qlbar use the finite-free local-triviality theorems; for OE use the local torsion charts and the two-term locally free resolution. The comparison concerns ordinary module sheaves, not completed coproducts.

For E and Qlbar, use equality Dctf=Dbc. The class Dic of complexes with ind-constructible cohomology contains Dbc and is triangulated, replete and closed under ambient sums, so the intersection universal property puts Loc(Dbc) inside Dic. Use the finite-subextension Qlbar coefficient object.

In these rational cases apply the proper unbounded-window sum theorem to families in Dic. Its comparison is the comparison defined by the coprojections, and restriction of the family gives the asserted preservation on Loc(Dbc).

For OE, choose a uniform finite upper bound d on the dimensions of geometric fibres. The integral direct-sum theorem gives the bound [0,2d+1] for ind-constructible sheaves, reduces each cohomology degree to the corresponding finite truncation window, and gives preservation on Loc(Dbc). Use only its direct-sum clauses, not any assertion that the bounded generators are compact.

In every certificate case the resulting image cocone is the colimit cocone because its canonical comparison is invertible. For the empty family this is the zero-to-zero comparison of an exact functor.
